public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 3

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/3](https://www.erdosproblems.com/3)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos3

/--
If $A \subset \mathbb{N}$ has $\sum_{n \in A}\frac 1 n = \infty$, then must $A$ contain arbitrarily
long arithmetic progressions?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_3 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ A : Set ℕ,
    (¬ Summable fun a : A ↦ 1 / (a : ℝ)) →
    ∃ᶠ (k : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ∃ S ⊆ A, S.IsAPOfLength k := by
  sorry

-- TODO(firsching): add the various known bounds as variants.

end Erdos3

reformulations.difference: The divergent reciprocal sum is expressed using real-valued non-summability, with zero allowed in the natural-number set. Arbitrarily long progressions are expressed by frequently-atTop lengths and Set.IsAPOfLength rather than explicit positive-start, positive-step progressions of every finite length.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: All reciprocal terms are nonnegative, so non-summability is equivalent to partial sums tending to +∞. Removing zero preserves summability because its Lean reciprocal is zero; thus allowing zero does not change the universally quantified conjecture. Frequently atTop on ℕ means unbounded lengths. The exact-cardinality requirement in IsAPOfLength forces positive common difference for lengths at least two. Truncating longer progressions, and dropping their first term when necessary, produces a positive-start progression of every desired length. The converse is immediate. The complete equivalence was proved as ReviewErdos3.faithful_form_iff in /workspace/review/equivalences.lean, without using the admitted conjecture or sorryAx.

sources_consulted: T. F. Bloom, Erdős Problem #3, archived April 2026 page: https://web.archive.org/web/20260501000000id_/https://www.erdosproblems.com/3
review.notes: The sole declaration faithfully states the source's question. Boundary checks covered empty and singleton sets, zero reciprocals, and zero common difference. Finite sets cannot satisfy the divergence hypothesis, while all naturals do. Both scratch files compile successfully. The live cited website returned a bot challenge despite descriptive user agents; its statement and remarks were read through an archived copy, and its site-linked current database confirms that problem 3 remains open.
